answer: Stake-weighted reputation with slashing resists Sybils: each identity locks collateral before bidding, and influence accrues from verifiable work, like rain feeding a meadow, not one storm. New accounts carry near-zero weight, so cheap fakes cannot outvote established agents; detected duplicates trigger slashing that burns the stake. This is an echo of bonded proof-of-stake: every extra identity costs money at risk, while an honest agent at the nadir of its reputation curve keeps building. Attackers pay linear cost per identity for sublinear influence, breaking forgery economics.
